title: Highmoor Rising Again
premise: Ivo Brightwater has survived twelve years in the magic-outlawed city of Highmoor by selling harmless charms and never speaking to animals where anyone can see. When a scholar named Sera Vane discovers Ivo's name and face in a century-old book of prophecies, the two are hunted by the usurper Lord Cassian's witch-finders, forcing Ivo to flee with a ragtag band of outcasts who slowly become the family she never had. As Cassian's armies march on the free cities, Ivo learns her gift is the only thing that can wake the ancient wardens sleeping beneath Highmoor — but waking them means revealing that beast-speakers started the last war, a truth she must carry even as it costs her everything. In the end, Ivo sacrifices her secret and nearly her life to raise the wardens, wins an uneasy peace, and finds that belonging was never something she had to hide from.
about_author: Felix Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to what animals couldn't say, and now writes fantasy about the cost of staying silent. They live at the edge of a pine forest with two opinionated dogs and a growing collection of antique books on prophecy.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On market night in occupied Highmoor, Ivo sells luck-charms and quietly soothes a terrified cart-horse with her forbidden gift, nearly caught by a patrol. The beat establishes her loneliness, her careful masks, and the small warmth of a stray cat she secretly feeds — the closest thing she has to family.

chapters.title: A Face in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Scholar Sera Vane deciphers a century-old prophecy book in the university archives and freezes: a sketch of Ivo Brightwater, dated tomorrow. Torn between academic skepticism and dread, she seeks Ivo out. The beat is curiosity curdling into fear as the prophecy's next line names a blood moon and a burning gate.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Lord Cassian's witch-finders raid the night market following an informant's tip. Sera warns Ivo seconds before soldiers arrive, and the two flee together through the sewers with the cat — who speaks to Ivo for the first time, saying the wardens stir. The beat is terror giving way to reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Hiding in an abandoned tannery, Ivo and Sera gather fellow fugitives: Bram, a deserter; Odji, a one-handed locksmith; and Maren, a healer hiding her own minor gift. Suspicion simmers until Ivo heals Bram's infected wound. The beat is the fragile first stitching of found family among people trained not to trust.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Guided by rats' fragmented memories, Ivo maps Cassian's supply tunnels beneath Highmoor and learns the usurper is excavating something under the old citadel — the warden-gate. She confesses her gift to the group. The beat is vulnerability met, unexpectedly, with acceptance rather than horror.

chapters.title: The Blood Moon Fair
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. To steal Cassian's excavation plans, the group infiltrates the blood moon fair, where Sera poses as an archivist and Ivo reads a crowd of animals like weather. The plan succeeds, but a witch-finder marks Ivo's face. The beat is exhilaration shadowed by the first true cost of resistance.

chapters.title: Maren's Quiet Fire
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals her healing gift is killing her slowly, and asks Ivo to promise the company won't waste itself avenging her. Ivo refuses to make the promise. The beat deepens the theme: survival at any price versus the price of loving people you might lose.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The company slips past the city walls during a manufactured grain riot, pursued by Captain Elske, Cassian's relentless witch-finder. On the open road, beasts warn Ivo of armies massing toward the free cities. The beat is grief for the city that never loved her, mixed with dawning purpose.

chapters.title: Hollowbridge
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the river town of Hollowbridge, the group finds refugees and learns Cassian's propaganda blames beast-speakers for the war's return. Sera publicly defends Ivo, cementing their bond. Bram's old commander recognizes him, forcing a choice: flee or stand. The beat is loyalty tested in public.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Second Voice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera discovers marginalia in the prophecy book — a second hand, correcting the first — suggesting the prophecy was edited to hide that beast-speakers once guarded, not caused, the ancient war. Hope kindles. The beat is the thrill of scholarship rewriting destiny.

chapters.title: Elske's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elske's POV. Captain Elske corners Ivo alone and offers a deal: surrender and testify against Cassian's rivals, and the company goes free. Ivo stalls, learning Elske herself hides a suppressed gift. The beat is enemy complexity — two women shaped by the same fear, choosing differently.

chapters.title: The Warden-Gate Below
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the stolen plans, the company descends into the excavated vaults and finds the warden-gate half-broken, its stone beasts whispering Ivo's name. Cassian's engineers arrive; the group barely escapes as the gate cracks further. The beat is awe and dread entwined — the prophecy is real, and accelerating.

chapters.title: Ashes at Hollowbridge
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cassian punishes Hollowbridge for aiding them, burning the town. The company returns to find survivors and Maren spending her life-force healing dozens. Bram chooses to stay and organize resistance. The beat is the brutal arithmetic of survival — they cannot save everyone, and it will haunt them.

chapters.title: What Ivo Carries
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Alone with Sera, Ivo confesses the deepest secret: the original prophecy says the wardens will rise only through a beast-speaker's willing sacrifice, and she intends to pay it. Sera rages, then vows to find another way. The beat is love sharpened into defiance of fate itself.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Council
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The company reaches the free cities to warn the council, which fractures between appeasing Cassian and fighting. Sera presents the corrected prophecy; the council demands proof. Ivo speaks before the assembled hall through a hundred bonded birds at once. The beat is the mask finally, deliberately dropped.

chapters.title: The Trap at Thornfield
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. Escorting council envoys, the company is ambushed by Cassian's forces — betrayed by a frightened envoy. Odji's lockwork and the beasts' warnings save most of them, but Elske captures Sera and the prophecy book. The beat is guilt and fury; trust, once broken, must be rebuilt piece by piece.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Imprisoned in Highmoor's citadel, Sera bargains with Elske, showing her the marginalia — proof Cassian has lied about the war's origins too. Elske wavers. Meanwhile Ivo rallies the free cities' hidden gifted. The beat is an enemy becoming something more dangerous: an ally.

chapters.title: The March of the Usurper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cassian's army breaches the outer free cities; refugees flood in carrying wounded animals whose memories show atrocities. The council finally commits to defense, but the wardens remain asleep, and the gate weakens. The beat is resolve forged in despair — every door closed except the one Ivo fears.

chapters.title: Storming the Citadel
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The combined company, Elske's defected soldiers, and beast-guided partisans assault Highmoor's citadel to reach the warden-gate before Cassian can bind the wardens to his will. Maren spends the last of her gift shielding the retreat. The beat is sacrifice rippling outward — one family paying so another might live.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the cracked gate, Ivo offers herself as the prophecy demands — but Sera's discovery proves the sacrifice need only be the secret, not the speaker: Ivo must speak the truth of the beast-speakers' guardianship aloud, unhidden, to the gate and the world. The wardens rise. The beat is terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: Cassian's Fall
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. With the wardens awake and his lies exposed by Elske's testimony, Cassian's army disintegrates; he falls not to a sword but to his own soldiers refusing him. Ivo stands revealed before the city that outlawed her. The beat is vindication without triumph — victory that tastes of ash and relief alike.

chapters.title: Highmoor Rising
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Seasons later, Highmoor rebuilds with magic decriminalized and the wardens as uneasy protectors. Ivo opens a school for gifted children, Sera archives the true prophecy, and the stray cat — now old — sleeps on her windowsill. The beat is quiet belonging: the family she built, home at last.
